claim: CodeVetter can compare two bounded same-runtime Next preflight requests with one uniquely correlated browser request and classify coarse timing shape without inventing compilation or source causation.

discarded_values: URL or route value in runtime evidence

proofs: Exactly two body-free GET observations share one bounded deadline.
Redirect, timeout, malformed, private-value, Vite, and unowned-listener cases fail closed.
Route, status-class, and unique browser-server identity must all match before comparison.
Every material classification is source-null, low-confidence, and edit-ineligible.

flow.name: home renders
flow.failure_boundary: The existing exact assertion did not pass before the bounded timeout; the timing shape remains diagnostic only.

comparison.interpretation: The first request was a material outlier, while both later observations remained expensive enough that initial-request effects do not explain the full latency.

diagnosis.result: The product surfaced the timing shape but did not call it compilation, name an application source, or authorize an optimization.

limitations: Two preflights and one browser request are a diagnostic sequence, not a latency distribution.
Preflight wall time and correlated server wall time use different observers.
A first-request outlier does not prove compilation, cache behavior, or exclusive work.
The local config-disabled Next development runtime does not establish repository-configured or production performance.
The existing Playwright assertion timed out, so this capture authorizes no source edit or optimization claim.
